nettle noun

also nettles, stinging nettle

classical

Catull. 44.15
Catull.
Hor.
Plin.

urtīca, urtīcae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Quantities follow Lewis & Short. For Catullus’s cold cured ōtiōque et urtīcā, see the cold.

Examples

  • Cavē urtīcās: urunt!

    Mind the nettles: they sting!composed

  • Urtīcā quid esse invīsius potest? at illa … vel plūrimīs scatet remediīs

    what could be more hateful than the nettle? yet it teems with remedies (the opening of Pliny’s chapter)Plin. NH 22.31

See also sea anemone, sting, cold, herbal tea.

SourcesLewis & Short: urtica

A classical word from Lewis & Short; neither Traupman nor Morgan–Owens has it in the sections swept.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.

Pliny (NH 22.31) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
